title: FRCS Ophthalmology: Viva & Clinical Masterclass
summary: A comprehensive compilation of high-yield clinical scenarios, VIVA topics, and examination techniques from the 2024-2025 FRCS Ophthalmology examinations. Essential knowledge for residents and fellows to master clinical reasoning and diagnostic precision.

rows: Determine acute vs chronic; Beta-blockers (Esmolol), Digoxin, Cardioversion (Electric/Amiodarone), Warfarin/Anticoagulation.
Suspect pituitary adenoma (chiasmatic lesion). Workup: Anterior/Posterior segment, Pupils, Confrontation VF, Automated Perimetry, MRI, Prolactin/Hormone assay.
Clinical tests, Pharmacological tests (Tensilon/Edrophonium test), Acetylcholine receptor antibodies, EMG single fiber.
Emergency: Paper bag breathing, Carbogen, Antiglaucoma, Ocular massage, Paracentesis, Carotid Doppler/Echocardiogram.
Monitor for Bull's eye maculopathy. Screening, baseline fundus, OCT, VF. Risk factor: Renal disease.

sections.title: Oculoplasty & Lid Pathology
content: Basal Cell Carcinoma: Rodent ulcer, full excision and reconstructive strategy.
Facial Nerve Palsy (Lagophthalmos): Temporary (Lubricants, taping), Permanent (Medial canthoplasty, lateral tarsorrhaphy, gold weight).
Orbital Cellulitis: Emergency admission, CBC/Temp, ENT consult, CT Orbit/Sinuses, rule out subperiosteal abscess.
Dermatochalasis/Ptosis Exam: MRD1, PFH, Levator function, Lid crease, Fatigability (30s look up), Ice test, Sleep test.

sections.title: Glaucoma Surgical Complications
content: Post-op Trabeculectomy Shallow AC + Low IOP: Rule out bleb leak (Seidel+), over-filtration, ciliary shutdown, or choroidal detachment.
Post-op Trabeculectomy + High IOP: Rule out pupillary block (transillumination), Suprachoroidal hemorrhage (B-scan), Malignant Glaucoma (Aqueous misdirection).
Malignant Glaucoma Management: Cycloplegics, YAG PI/capsulotomy, Vitrectomy.

rows: Cataract surgery, guarded visual prognosis, monitor for glaucoma/retinal detachment.

sections.title: Exam Pearls: Differential Diagnosis
sections.content: For Lateral Rectus Palsy: Always investigate systemic health (Diabetes/HTN/Lipids), Neuroimaging, and look for progression. Post-6 months: Strabismus surgery or Botulinum toxin (though limited by medial rectus restriction). For Phthisis Bulbi: Chronic endophthalmitis or severe trauma; consider colored contact lenses, prosthetic shell, or evisceration for volume loss.
